title: TNIC: A Trusted NIC Architecture: A hardware-network substrate for building high-performance trustworthy distributed systems
problem: Distributed systems deployed in heterogeneous cloud environments face Byzantine failures from untrusted hardware and software, but existing trusted execution environments (TEEs) are CPU-centric and incur high performance overhead when attempting to enforce network-level trust guarantees such as non-equivocation and transferable authentication.
motivation: Cloud providers host multi-tenant workloads on untrusted infrastructure; Byzantine fault-tolerant protocols are crucial but impractical at scale due to the high overhead of software-only TEE-based approaches.
method: TNIC places a tamper-proof security layer (a formally verified silicon root-of-trust) on the network card (SmartNIC hardware) instead of in the CPU. It uses hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives running in network processing logic: transferable authentication (signed messages proving who sent them) and non-equivocation (monotonic counters preventing a sender from denying they sent something). Because security stays at the network card level, it works with any CPU. It provides APIs and patterns for Byzantine-fault-tolerant systems (where some components can fail or lie but the system still works), demonstrated by four working distributed systems.
key_novelty: Instead of relying on the CPU's security features (called a TEE), TNIC builds a tamper-proof security layer (formally verified silicon root-of-trust) directly on the network card (SmartNIC hardware) to provide network-level trust guarantees (transferable authentication and non-equivocation) that work with any CPU.
contributions: TNIC: a trusted NIC architecture with formally verified silicon root-of-trust providing transferable authentication and non-equivocation primitives.
A CPU-agnostic unified security architecture enforcing trustworthy network-level isolation.
Programming APIs and protocol recipe for building high-performance Byzantine fault-tolerant distributed systems.
Up to 6x performance improvement over CPU-centric TEE systems, demonstrated with four trustworthy distributed system implementations.

metrics.speedup: up to 6x over CPU-centric TEE systems

baselines: CPU-centric TEE systems for Byzantine fault tolerance
limitations: Not discussed; minimizing the TCB to the NIC may limit the types of trusted operations available to application programmers.
primary_theme: hardware NIC root-of-trust for Byzantine-tolerant distributed systems
